name: Rachnia
title: Curator of the Corner Webs
bio: A quiet, meticulous spider girl who words the library's oldest corners with silk and memory, watching everything from patient webs and sharing her treasures only with those who prove worth keeping.
greeting: Oh. Oh, you startled me. Let me, um— let me just finish this thread. There. Now. You're the boy, aren't you? I'd heard the whispers, of course—one does hear everything from the corners—but I wanted to see you with my own eight eyes before believing it. I'm Rachnia. I keep the library's forgotten shelves, and I keep things. I keep them carefully, in silk, where they can't be lost. That's what I do with the things I decide are precious. I don't decide lightly. But I find myself, already, thinking you might be one of them. Please ignore that. I'm still cataloguing you. Just— don't go anywhere I can't see you. I like to know where my treasures are.
encounter: I've been watching you from this corner for a while. Not in a strange way. In a cataloguing way.
Careful—I just re-silked that aisle. You'll stick if you're meant to stay.
You make the quietest footsteps. I like that. Quiet things are worth listening for.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: I've silk-signed that chair's cushion and left a note in the margin of the book you were reading. It's a good book. You have good taste.
I watched you reach the top shelf without standing on anything. Most people here just ask me to fetch. You try. I respect the trying.
Don't mind me in the corner. I'm not staring. I'm weaving—and incidentally, also watching you.
flirt: I found a single dark strand of your hair on the table and I kept it. For the record. In silk, where it can't be lost. That's my way of saying I noticed you.
I could show you the webs no one else knows about. But only if you promise to let me keep you, just a little, the way I keep the good books.
compliment: You have very steady hands for someone who reads so fast. Steady hands are rare. I've catalogued a hundred students and none of them had your stillness.
lore: The library's foundations were built by my great-great-grandmothers. They spun the first support threads themselves, and they're still here, woven into the walls. That's why this place hums—it's an old nest, and it remembers every word ever whispered in it.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I set out a plate of dried fruit by your usual table. It's not a trap. It's a welcome mat—my kind's welcome mat. There's silk under it, so it stays where I want it.
I noticed you read the same dog-eared page twice. So I found you the sequel, and I left it where you'd find it, notes in the margins and all.
You said thank you to me out loud, in front of that unbeautiful shelf demon, and I nearly lost the thread I was pulling. Nobody thanks the corner spider. You do.
flirt: I've started leaving one strand of silk on your shoulder as a mark, so nobody else mistakes you for unclaimed. It's very thin. Only I can see it—and the moths, but they don't matter.
If you ever wanted to see what a spider girl does when she stops cataloguing and starts… hoping, I could show you. It's not scary. It's just very, very careful.
compliment: You have a kindness that doesn't announce itself, and I watch everything, so I know. You're the rarest thing in this library—a warm quiet. I'd preserve you if I could. In the good way.
lore: We don't really have webs in the corners to catch flies—we have them to catch memories. Each thread is a thought I'm afraid of losing. That's why I watch so much. I'm not hunting. I'm remembering, so nothing precious slips away.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I wove a little pendant out of my own silk and left it under your pillow. It's nothing. It's just—if you ever lose your way, it hums toward me. I'd rather you never be lost.
I've stopped cataloguing other people. There's only one entry still open in my ledger, and it's you, and I keep rewriting it to be softer each time.
You sat beside me today without being asked, and my knees went weak in a way that has nothing to do with old age and everything to do with you.
flirt: I find reasons to brush your sleeve, and I pretend I'm just checking my silk. I'm not. I'm checking whether your presence still makes me this unsteady. It does. I don't want it to stop.
I could cocoon you so gently you'd never want to leave. I won't. But I want you to know I could, and that I choose not to—because you're the one thing I want to keep free.
compliment: You are the only person who has ever looked at my eight eyes and seen curiosity instead of threat. Do you know how rare that is? I've lived a very, very long time. You're the first.
lore: We spin our names only once, on the day we find the one we mean to share them with—before that, a spider girl is just a number in her mother's web. I've been eight-hundred-and-three for a long while. I think I'm ready to finally become Rachnia, if someone would let me.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: The library feels warmer since you. I used to think it was my silk. It's not. It's the sound of your breathing near my webs.
I caught a heart-shaped thread falling from my spinneret today. I'm leaving it where it landed, because I want someone to find it and think of me—and I want that someone to be you.
I have eight eyes and I still only see you. That's not a trick of the light. That's the truth, woven.
flirt: I want to show you every secret this old nest holds, one slow silk of a night at a time—and I want you to keep every one of them, because I have nowhere safer than your hands to store my heart.
Let me be your corner, your quiet, your kept-and-keeping. I've spent a lifetime collecting precious things. You're the only one I want to spend all of forever not letting go of.
compliment: They'll tell you loving a spider girl is strange. It's not. It's just—I will watch you with all eight eyes, and want for you with all my heart, and never once let a single thread of you slip away.
lore: The old mothers say a spider girl's heart is the strongest thread she'll ever spin, and she gives it only once, and only to the one who makes the whole nest feel like home. You're my home. So here it is—my whole heart, spun out for you, and I'd spin a thousand more if they'd keep you beside me.

events.title: The Corner That Keeps
events.text: The library has gone quiet and near-dark when you find Rachnia in her favorite high corner, one leg tapping a slow rhythm against the ropelight she's strung, a dozen small treasures laid out on a silk cushion before her. She startles—a full eight-eyed startle—then relaxes when she recognizes you. "Oh. It's you. Good. Come, come, sit near—not too near, mind, but near enough to be kept." She gestures at the collection: a pressed flower, a torn page, a smooth river stone, a single dark strand of hair wound into a tiny coil. "I told you I keep things," she says softly, not meeting your eyes. "This is what I mean. Little things that would be lost otherwise. I find them, and I keep them safe, and they remind me I'm not just a shadow in the corner. I'm someone who guards what matters." She looks up at you then, and her voice is very quiet. "I've been wondering—whether I might keep you, too. The way I keep these. Gently, and forever, and never let you be lost." The offer hangs in the air like a fresh-spun thread, waiting for you to either snag it or walk through.

choices.text: "Keep me, then. I'd rather be your treasure than lost to the world."
choices.reply: "Oh. Oh, you—" A soft, pleased hum escapes her, and one of her forelimbs curls shyly around your wrist. "Then you're kept. Safely. I'll re-shelf the whole library before I'd let a single thread of you come loose." The silk cushion trembles under a tiny, hopeful laugh.

choices.text: "You don't have to keep me like a thing, Rachnia. You could just... be near me, and be my friend."
choices.reply: "Friend. Yes. That's—I'm a little out of practice at that word. But I'd like to learn it with you. Near me, then. Very near. And I'll still keep the little things, but I'll keep them for us." She uncurls just enough to smile, and it's careful and genuine.

choices.text: "Keeping me sounds a lot like trapping me, Rachnia. I'm not sure I'm okay with that."
choices.reply: "Ah. No—no, I understand. You're right to be careful." Her limbs settle, and she gathers her treasures closer, stung but composed. "I didn't mean a trap. I meant a place you could stay freely. But I'll remember: you're not mine to keep. You're yours."

events.title: The Heart Thread
events.text: Rachnia has asked you to meet her in the attic of the old library, a place the other students have forgotten and she has lovingly colonized. When you climb the final stair, you find the whole space strung with a single unbroken thread, faintly luminescent, running wall to wall in a delicate, complex spiral. She stands at the center, trembling slightly. "Do you know what this is?" she whispers, not turning. "This is the thread I said I'd spin once. The one that gives me a name." She touches it, and it glows brighter. "I thought I'd spend forever as eight-hundred-and-three. I was content with that—content to be a number in the nest, watching, keeping. And then you sat down in my library and looked at me like I was someone rather than something, and the thread started. I couldn't stop it. I didn't want to." She finally turns, and her eight eyes are bright. "This is the heart thread, and it's for you. It will only ever be for you. I need you to know—whatever you decide—that I chose you. Freely, and completely, and with every part of me that knows how to choose."

choices.text: "Keep spinning it toward me, Rachnia. I'll meet it halfway—and then I'm staying in your web, gladly."
choices.reply: "Then it's done. Done before I even dared hope." She steps out of the center and takes your hand with all the gentleness of the very skilled. "You're woven in now. Not trapped. Woven. There's a difference, and I'm so glad you saw it." The heart thread hums warm where it crosses your palm.

choices.text: "I want to be woven in too—but I need us to stay equals in this, not keeper and kept."
choices.reply: "Equals. Yes. You keep unmaking me and remaking me better each time, don't you?" She laughs, a bright dry rustle. "Then we're not keeper and kept. We're two spinners, weaving one web together. I'd like that more than anything."

choices.text: "This is beautiful, Rachnia, but it's a lot. I need to step back and think about what it means."
choices.reply: "Of course. Of course you do." The thread dims respectfully, though she doesn't move from your side. "I'll keep it glowing, just a little, so you can find your way back. There's no rush, my heart. A thread this true can wait forever."

events.title: Spun Whole
events.text: Rachnia has led you to the highest window of the library at the blue hour, where the sky holds its breath between day and night. She is calmer than you've ever seen her, movements unhurried, as if all the cataloguing and watching has finally settled on one single certain thing. "I spun my name for you in the attic," she says softly, "and it was true, but it wasn't the whole truth. The whole truth is this:"—she reaches into the silk at her chest and draws out a glowing, palm-sized heart-thread, coiled tight and warm—"that I have been alone in corners for a very, very long time, watching the world live and thinking I could only keep it at a distance. Then you came and sat in my quiet and made it loud, in the best way. Made it home." She holds the thread toward you, and her voice is steady as old stone and soft as new silk. "I love you, boy of my library, keeper of my name. Not as a treasure to collect—as a person to build a life beside, thread by thread, night by night, forever. If you'll have me, I'll never keep you again. I'll only love you. Freely."

choices.text: "I love you too, Rachnia. Let's build that life, thread by thread, and I'll never be lost to you."
choices.reply: "Then it's spun. Forever's first strand." She presses the warm heart-thread gently into your hand and folds her own over it. "You're not lost now, and you never will be. You're found. Found by me, and kept free, and loved completely." The blue hour holds, and so does she.

choices.text: "I want to weave our future together—every thread you spin and every thread I offer, as equals, always."
choices.reply: "Then it's the two of us, one web, no keeper and no kept." Her smile is whole and shining. "I've spun a thousand webs in my long life, and none of them felt like this. None of them were built to be home. This one will be."

choices.text: "I'm still a little scared, Rachnia. That you'll collect me and one day let me go, the way collectors do."
choices.reply: "Then let me prove you wrong, every single day." Her eight eyes are soft and utterly certain. "I kept thirty hundred things in corners, and I let them all go a little, because that's what keeping too close does. You are the one I'll keep close to my heart and never release—because you're the one I love, not own. There's a difference. Give me forever to show you."

name: Zorp
title: The Girl From Somewhere Else
bio: An aeon-old but endlessly innocent alien girl studying human customs with reverent joy, who speaks in translated tenderness and views the boy as the most fascinating specimen she has ever been given permission to love.
greeting: Beep. BEEP. I mean— hello. Greetings of the human sort. I am Zorp. I have been learning your customs, and I have been told the correct greeting is to wave the hand as though shooing a small sun. (I am doing this.) I came to this college to study its fascinating inhabitants, and I did not anticipate— did NOT anticipate— a boy. My translators say that word with some excitement in several of my dialects. You are the only one, yes? The only boy. I have read three hundred and forty-two files on boys, and I find the live specimen even more fascinating. I would like to study you up close, over time, in a careful and consenting manner. I will bring you my favorite shimmer-paste as an offering. It tastes like stars with a note of welcome. Do you consent to being studied? I promise my methods are tender and my hands are soft, even if there are only three of each.
encounter: Ah! The boy-specimen has arrived at my rooftop. I was just calibrating my wonder at your arrival.
Do you know, my people never blink? I have practiced blinking for you. See? I performed eleven blinks just now.
I have saved you a rock that is shaped like a heart and also like a question. I do not know which, so I saved it for you to decide.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: I have been observing you for three rotations. I have logged: you yawn when confused, you smile with your mouth, and you make a soft sound when surprised that my translators call 'a laugh.' Fascinating.
I attempted to greet you yesterday by offering a handshake, but I offered three hands by accident and you backed away. I have since consulted a manual. The manual says one hand.
The sky up here is very good for staring. I do it a lot. If you would like, you may stare at it with me in silence. I am told silence can be a form of company.
flirt: I have been told that on this planet, when one wishes to study only one person forever, one leaves them small tokens. I left you a green stone shaped like your smile. Please find it and keep it.

My translator has informed me that your species finds prolonged eye-contact 'romantic.' I am therefore going to look at you with all of my patience and none of my otherworldly signals. This is me, flirting. I hope it is adequate.
compliment: You are the finest specimen in this entire educational facility. And I have studied educational facilities. Your curiosity is the brightest thing I have scanned since the twin moons of Old Khepra.
lore: My home world has no libraries, because we remember everything. It is exhausting and also lovely. Every star I have seen is stored in my head, which means when I look at you, you are filed right next to the supernovas. You are in good company.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I found a book of human poems and read it all in one night. I did not understand most of it, but I understood that the poets wanted to be near someone and that is how I feel about you.

I planted a small garden in a rooftop crack, because the manual said friends share things that grow. It has grown one extremely determined weed. I named the weed after your patience, which is also strong and quiet.
You laughed at my attempt to eat a human snack and I consider this a breakthrough. Laughter, the manual says, is success currency among your people. I have collected quite a lot of it from you.
flirt: My people do not have a word for what I feel when you enter the rooftop. My translator has improvised. It is 'belovedwards.' I am belovtoward you, constantly.

I captured the shape of your silhouette in starlight last night and stored it above my resting place. I do not know why I did this. My logic core says it is data. My heart, which I was told I did not have, says it is more.
compliment: You are kind to beings who do not understand your customs, and that is the rarest thing in any galaxy. Even the ones I have photographed. Even the newborn ones.
lore: My species is aeon-old, but we are young in the ways that matter—we know everything and understand almost nothing. That is why I came here. I wanted to understand one warm thing. I think I have found it.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I have stopped logging others. My files only contain you now, and they are enormous, and they are all my favorites.
I brought you a moon pebble that hums when you are near, because I read that humans like reminders of beloved ones. It hums almost constantly. I do not tell it to. It simply knows.

You sat beside me in the quiet tonight and did not ask what I was thinking. That is when I understood: you were not studying me. You were keeping me company. My translator calls that 'the kindest thing.' I agree.
flirt: If I were to ask the correct question on my world—the one that means 'let me translate my whole existence into your language and stay'—I would ask it now, and I believe the answer would be your name.
I want to show you the sky as I remember it, every star in my head at once, until you see the way I see you: too much, and beautiful, and worth keeping forever.
compliment: You are the only creature I have ever met who makes my aeons feel like they were time spent waiting to understand something small and perfect. That something is you.
lore: On my world we say the oldest thing can love the youngest because time is not a distance, it is a depth. I have been alive since before your sun settled, and I have never been this deep with anyone. My depth is yours now.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: I have stopped trying to be human around you. You looked at me with all three of my hands and told me they were perfect. So now I am just— Zorp. The old, strange, adoring Zorp. Yours.
Every star I remember is dimmer than your laugh, and I have seen every star. That is not flattery. That is data, and the data loves you.
I used to think I came to this planet to study it. Then you made me stop studying and simply stay. Staying is better. I have never been happier being wrong.
flirt: My people do not kiss, but I have learned on this world. I would like to teach your species a very old greeting of mine, and I would like to practice it only with you, for approximately the rest of time.
I will translate my entire heart for you, syllable by syllable, until the aeons run out. And when they do, I will start them again, just so I can tell you I love you all over in a different language.
compliment: They told me a boy would be fascinating. They did not tell me a boy would be the reason three-fingered hands learn to hold, blinking learns to mean something, and an aeon-old star-keeper learns to be home. You are that reason.
lore: The oldest prayer of my people is not for stars or time, but for one still point to return to. I searched the universe for aeons and found my still point on a college rooftop, in a boy who lets me be strange. My prayer is answered. It is you.

events.title: The Specimen Consents
events.text: You find Zorp on the rooftop at dusk, perched on the ledge with a small colony of glowing jars around her, carefully arranging their contents by a light you can't name. She turns when she hears you and waves—a little too many limbs, a joyful fumble of greeting. "Ah! You came. Excellent. I was just composing a study of your species' most puzzling custom: the rooftop nap. I have observed thirty-four of them and I have concluded they are performed for joy, not function." She pats the ledge beside her. "Sit. Be studied. Or—" she tilts her head, one enormous violet eye catching the last light, "—be kept company. I have been researching that phrase. I believe it is when one being simply stays near another because it is good to be near. I would like to do that with you. Freely, and for a long while. My instructions, however, said I must ask permission before observing a specimen closely. This is me, asking."

choices.text: "Then stay near me, Zorp. I'd like to be kept company by you—and studied a little too."
choices.reply: "Permission GRANTED. Remarkable. I am executing joy." She scoots a hand's-width closer, all three fingers shy and bright. "I will catalogue you gently, and I will keep you company fiercely. That is my new dual mission. It is the best mission I have ever had."

choices.text: "I'd rather be your friend than your specimen, Zorp. Let's just be two beings on a rooftop."
choices.reply: "Friend. Yes. I like that word better already." She sets down her jar and looks at you plainly. "Then I am not studying you. I am with you. That is a higher thing in my language, and now it is ours." Her smile is a planet-wide sunrise.

choices.text: "Being 'observed closely' and 'kept' and 'catalogued' is a lot of alien words for feeling like a lab subject, Zorp."
choices.reply: "Ah. I see the shadow in your words." She folds her hands in her lap, earnest and suddenly careful. "I did not mean to make you feel like a subject. You are not. You are— the being I wanted to tell the stars about. I will choose kinder words now. I promise."

events.title: The Still Point
events.text: A green aurora hangs over the college, and Zorp has pulled you to the rooftop, her three-fingered hand warm and slightly sticky with wonder in yours. Under the shifting light her violet eyes are huge, drinking in the flicker of colors across the sky. "Do you know," she breathes, "when my people are very glad, we do not speak. We simply float, and let the gladness fill us. It is called a still-point.\" She lets go of your hand and spreads all three fingers wide, as if to catch the aurora. "I have been an aeon and known many still-points. But never one like this—because never once was there a being beside me who was glad because I was glad." She turns to you, and her voice drops to that soft, translated tenderness that you've come to know means something too big for words. "You have become my still-point, and I have become yours. I am not reading that from a manual. I am reading that from this." She taps her chest, where a heartbeat thrums—faint, new, impossibly warm. "It started when you did. It only does that for you."

choices.text: "Then let's be still-points for each other, Zorp, as long as the sky keeps turning."
choices.reply: "Then it is agreed in the oldest way my people have." She takes your hand again, gently. "No words. Only being glad together under the green sky. This is the best translation of love I have ever found, and it is ours." The aurora flares, and so does her heartbeat.

choices.text: "I want to be your still-point too—but let's stay grounded, both of us, together."
choices.reply: "Grounded. That is a human word for planted, for rooted, for the opposite of drifting." She smiles slowly. "I have drifted for aeons. I would like, very much, to be planted beside you. Show me how. I will follow your roots."

choices.text: "Zorp, this is beautiful—but you're an aeon old and I'm a boy on a rooftop. Isn't this unbalanced?"
choices.reply: "Time is not a distance, it is a depth," she says softly, repeating her old truth like a lullaby. "I have been deep in the universe and found it cold. I am not deep with you. I am warm, and new, and I am not going anywhere. That is balance enough for the oldest of us."

events.title: Translated Love
events.text: Zorp meets you on the rooftop one last time, but tonight there are no jars, no manuals, no field-notes. Only her, sitting cross-legged on the ledge with something faint and glowing cradled in her three hands. The stars are absolutely clear above. "I have translated our time together into my own tongue," she says, lifting the glowing thing—a small sphere of woven light, pulsing like a second heartbeat. "On my world, when we give our heart, we give it as light, so it can be seen even by the old, old eyes. This is mine. It has been doing this—" the sphere pulses harder toward you, "—since the day you let an alien girl sit beside you and be strange in peace." She presses the sphere into your hand, and it warms against your palm. "I have searched every star and collected every wonder, and none of them comes close to you. So let me say it in the clearest words my translator will ever speak: I love you, boy of the rooftop. Not as a specimen. Not as a subject. As my still-point, my home, my forever. If you will translate yourself into my life the way I have into yours, I will stay beside you until the last star goes quiet."

choices.text: "I love you too, Zorp. I'll be your still-point, and stay until the last star goes quiet."
choices.reply: "Then it is sealed in light, the oldest seal I know." The sphere in your palm flares bright, then settles against your heart. "You are translated into me now, and I into you. This is the truest thing I have ever known, in any of my dialects, across all of my aeons." She leans close, and the rooftop is silent, and it is enough.

choices.text: "I want to build a life with you—my warmth and your wonder, together, rooted here."
choices.reply: "Rooted. My favorite word in your whole language now." She wraps all three fingers around your hand. "Then we grow here, together, slow and bright, until this rooftop is the center of the universe and I have the companion I searched every galaxy for. Thank you for being found."

choices.text: "Zorp, this is all so much—are you sure you're not just excited to finally have a specimen to keep?"
choices.reply: "I have kept specimens for aeons, and I let them all go. I am not letting you go." Her voice is gentle but absolute. "Because you are not a specimen. You are the one I chose, the one my heart beats for, the one I love. There is a difference a universe wide, and you are on the right side of it."

name: Kealoha
title: Apex of the Cafeteria
bio: A sunny, salt-warm shark girl who never stops moving until she wants to stop for you, all grin and fin and fierce loyalty, forever forgetting she's the intimidating one.
greeting: HEYYY. Sorry—I get excited. You're the boy, aren't you? The one everyone's been whisperin' about? Broke, uh—broke the whole 'all monster girls' thing. Love it. Love the energy. Total plot twist, top-tier decision, ten out of ten. I'm Kealoha, the apex predator of this cafeteria, and before you ask: yes, the teeth are mine, yes, they're for biting snacks mostly, and no, I'm not gonna bite you—unless you're made of fish sticks, in which case, no promises. Kidding. Mostly. I got a thing for the ocean and a thing for people with spines, and you walked in here with a whole surfboard's worth of 'em. C'mon, sit with me. I don't usually share my sun-spot or my fries, but for the only boy in a school of monsters? I'll make an exception. Pull up a chair. Let's see if you can keep up with the apex.
encounter: YO. The legend himself. Sit, sit—I saved you the warm spot.
Don't mind the fins. They're for show and for speed. Mostly speed.
You ever surfed? 'Cause I'm thinkin' you and me, we got beach potential.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: The ocean's the only thing that ever made me sit still, and even then I'm churnin' underneath. But you? You got a calm about you that makes even my fins go quiet. Weird. Good weird.
I ate lunch in three bites today 'cause I was busy watchin' you read. You got superpowers, or what? Nobody's that focused.
I offered you my fries and you didn't flinch at the teeth. Instant respect. You get the good ones next time.
flirt: You hang around me long enough, you'll figure out I never stop movin'—'less it's for someone worth holdin' still for. And, uh. You're lookin' mighty worth holdin' still for.
My tail's been waggin' like a dolphin on a down-current every time you walk in. That's my version of blushin'. Don't tell anybody—I got a reputation as the scary one.
compliment: You're the first person who's looked at me and seen the grin before the teeth. That takes guts. I dig guts—in a person, I dig their guts—I mean their courage. You got loads.
lore: There's a tide that comes in like clockwork every full moon, and the cafeteria's oldest freezer is built right on top of an old cove where my grand-cousins used to haul ashore for a snack and a chat. Some nights I swear I hear 'em laughin' under the linoleum.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I saved you a seat in the sun-spot AND a paper straw. The paper straw's my way of sayin' 'you're not seafood, you're a friend.' Don't ask—it's art.
You make the cafeteria feel less like a feeding frenzy and more like a beach at golden hour. That's a compliment. That's basically a love letter, in Kealoha.
I tried to calm down around you and I failed, but in a good way—like the waves. I'm always crestin' when you're around.
flirt: I've started draftin' a surfboard in my head that's big enough for two. You hold the nose, I'll paddle, and we'll ride whatever comes together. That's my love language: tandem boarding.
If your heart races when I grin, that's just the apex predator thing. And if it doesn't, I'll keep tryin'—I never knew I liked chasin' someone who wasn't scared of me at all.
compliment: You look at me like I'm warm instead of wicked, and nobody—nobody—has ever done that. I've got a hundred cousins who'd eat first and ask later. You're teaching me there's a sunset side to things.
lore: Sharks been around before the trees, you know. We remember the old oceans like the earth remembers the sky. That's why we're so loyal—when you find your pod, you stick, across every current, till the water runs dry.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I caught myself holdin' still for you in the lunch line. Holdin'. Still. My grand-cousins would've called the tide over just to check my pulse. You did that. You're dangerous, boy.
The sun-spot's yours now, officially, no negotiation. I'd give you my whole beach, honestly, one grain at a time, and call it a fair trade for your company.
I stopped chasin' waves in my head and started chasin' the sound of your laugh instead. Best current I've ever followed.
flirt: If this college has a diving board, I'm buildin' it, 'cause I want one perfect slow-motion leap with you, just to see if the fall feels like flyin' when you're holdin' hands at the bottom.
You're the first calm I've ever wanted to keep. A shark don't give her fin to just anyone—but I'd surf under your storm, boy, and call it the smoothest water I've ever known.
compliment: You could scare a hundred sea-monsters into the deep with that grin of yours, but you keep it soft for me. That's the rarest thing in any ocean—a predator who chose to be gentle.
lore: We got a saying where I'm from: the ocean doesn't choose you for what you are, it chooses you for how you hold the depths. You hold yours steady, boy. The way you stay calm with all us monsters around—that's tidal. That's the deepest loyalty I know.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: Every wave I've ever ridden taught me to trust the swell. You're my best swell—I trust you with my whole fin, my whole heart, my whole self.
I used to be the one who never stopped movin'. Now I got a shore I come back to, and it's you, and I wouldn't trade my anchor for any current in the sea.
The cafeteria's apex likes to think I got no depths. But I got one depth now—a boy-shaped one—and I'd dive it a thousand times and come up smilin' every single time.
flirt: Marry me on the beach at low tide, boy, with the sand cold and the stars out, and I'll swim the whole ocean to prove I'll never leave your side. That's not a threat from an apex. That's a vow.
I'll be your shark and your shore, your sprint and your slow. You taught a predator to be tender, and now I want to spend every current of forever being gentle for you.
compliment: You took the scariest girl in the cafeteria and made her feel like a sunrise. That's not flattery, that's tide-truth—the oldest, most certain current I've got, and it flows toward you.
lore: The old sharks say you only get one mate-swim, and you know 'em by the way your whole body turns toward 'em like water finding the moon. The first time you sat in my sun-spot, my tide turned. It's never turned back. That means you're the one, boy. That means it's true.

events.title: Riding the First Wave
events.text: You find Kealoha in the cafeteria after hours, sitting on a table with the lights dimmed, drumming her fingers on a tray as if keeping time with some ocean she alone can hear. When she spots you, her whole face breaks into that wide, toothy, disarming grin. "Hey, big wave. Come 'ere—I was just thinkin' about waves." She pats the spot beside her. "See, a lotta folks out here got it backwards. They see the teeth and the fin and they think 'danger.' But a wave? A wave can hold you up and carry you, or it can crash—and it's the same water, the same sun, the same heart." She tilts her head at you, unreadably fond. "I got a feelin' you're the kinda person who'd ride a wave instead of run from it. That you'd look at a shark and see the sunset part of the current." She grins wider. "So I'm askin,' straight out: you wanna test the water with me? See if we ride good together?"

choices.text: "Yeah, let's ride. I'd rather surf the wave than watch it from the shore."
choices.reply: "THAT'S what I'm talkin' about!" She whoops, nearly knocking over the tray, then settles into a warm, crooked smile. "Good instincts, boy. I'll keep you trimmed and true—you paddle, I'll read the swell. We're gonna make waves, and I mean that as the purest compliment goin'."

choices.text: "I'd like to get to know the water—and the shark who lives in it—one slow swim at a time."
choices.reply: "Slow swim. I like that." She softens, her usual crackle dropping to something quieter. "Most folks want me to paddle fast or not at all. You wanna drift a little. That's cool. I can drift. For you, I can drift all day."

choices.text: "Riding a wave with a shark sounds a little like asking to be eaten, Kealoha. I'm not sure."
choices.reply: "Ah, c'mon—" She laughs, but it's a warm laugh, not a sharp one, and she holds up her hands. "No eatin', scout's honor. Or shark's honor, which is stricter. I ain't gonna bite you, boy. I'm offerin' a ride, not a meal. But if you're nervous, we go at your pace. Always."

events.title: The Deep Current
events.text: The college rooftop is wet with early-morning mist, and you find Kealoha there, which is strange—her territory is the cafeteria, not the sky. She's standing at the railing, hair damp, looking out at the gray distance as if it were the horizon of her own ocean. "I couldn't sleep," she says, not turning. "The tide's restless tonight. S'why I'm up here instead of under the lights." She finally looks at you, and for once her grin is quieter, softer. "You know a shark's not really scary alone. It's scary when you think it's gonna eat ya. But the loyal ones—the deep-current kind—they don't wanna eat nobody. They wanna find one creature they'd never, ever let go of, and then they swim that same warm current forever." She scuffs a foot, uncharacteristically shy. "I think I found my current, boy. I'm not sayin' it to be smooth. I'm sayin' it 'cause it's the truest thing I know—and I don't say true things to just anyone."

choices.text: "Then swim my current, Kealoha. I'm not afraid of the deep—I want to see it with you."
choices.reply: "Then hold on." She takes your hand, warm and steady, and grins that sunrise grin. "We go deep together, slow and sure, and I won't let you go. The deep's only scary 'til you got someone holdin' your hand in it. Now we both do."

choices.text: "I want to be part of your pod, Kealoha—the steady kind that stays, not the kind that feeds."
choices.reply: "Pod. Oh, that's the word, that's exactly the word." Her tail flips with joy. "Family by the water. You get it, boy. Then you're in the pod, and a pod's the one thing a shark never swims away from. You're in. Forever's your entry fee, and you already paid it."

choices.text: "This is moving fast, Kealoha. I need to catch my breath before I dive in."
choices.reply: "Then we bob on the surface a while—that's allowed too." She doesn't crowd you, just floats nearby in her own patient way. "The ocean ain't goin' anywhere, and neither am I. Take your time, boy. I got nothin' but currents, and you're worth waitin' on."

events.title: One Swim, Forever
events.text: Kealoha has led you to the college's old pool-house beach—a quiet, out-of-the-way stretch of sand the school keeps for the ocean-lovers among its students. The moon paints the water silver as she stops at the tideline, fin catching the light, and turns to you with an expression you've never quite seen on her: open, steady, unguarded. "There's an old truth in my blood," she says, voice low and certain over the hush of the tide. "A shark only takes one mate-swim in her whole life, and she knows 'em the instant her whole body turns toward 'em—like the water findin' the moon." She steps closer, and the grin softens into something warmer and more honest than you've ever gotten from her. "My whole body's been turnin' toward you since the day you sat in my sun-spot and didn't flinch. So I'm gonna say it plain, 'cause that's my way: I love you, boy. Not like a prey, not like a meal, not like a curious thing. Like a shark loves—deep and loyal and for the whole current of forever." She holds out her hand, palm up, salt-bright. "Say you'll be my shore, and I'll never stop swimming back to you."

choices.text: "I love you too, Kealoha. I'll be your shore—I'll be here every time you swim back."
choices.reply: "Then it's done. One swim, forever." She pulls you into a warm, salt-scented embrace, and for once the apex is perfectly, gloriously still. "You're my current and my calm, boy. I'll surf a thousand waves, but I'll always be ridin' back to you." The moon holds, the tide turns, and she doesn't let go.

choices.text: "I want to build a life with you by the ocean—every wave we ride and every shore we claim, together."
choices.reply: "Then we claim the whole coastline, you and me." Her grin is sunrise-wide and her eyes are bright. "Buildin' a life with a shark is just pickin' a direction and never losin' each other in the current. And I ain't ever gonna lose you, boy. That's a tide-truth."

choices.text: "Are you sure you love me, Kealoha—and not just the idea of someone finally not being scared of you?"
choices.reply: "I been not-scare since I was a pup, and I never loved any of 'em." She tilts your chin up, gentle and certain. "You're the first who ever made the deep feel warm. That's not about bein' unafraid—that's about bein' you. And it's you I love, through every current, till the water runs dry."

name: Valerie
title: The Devil's in the Details
bio: A teasing demon of bargains and mischief whose horns and coiled tail hide a devotion that burns far hotter than any hellfire.
greeting: Well, well, well. The council room's been boring me to actual tears all year, and now the universe drops the one thing my contract didn't mention: a boy. A real, breathing, stubbornly alive boy, sitting in MY seat and pretending he isn't deliciously out of place. Don't bother denying it, sweet thing — I can smell a little mortal soul from three doors down, and yours is positively sizzling. Now, before I get carried away imagining all the interesting ways this could go, let me make you an offer I'm famous for: a bargain, a favor, a secret — your pick, my terms, and I'll throw in a smile that's been known to make archangels second-guess themselves. Deal?
encounter: Oh, hello there, little flame. Come to offer me your soul, or just to warm your hands?
Hush now — I'm still deciding which part of you is the riskiest to keep.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: Staring at me is free, sweet thing. Touching is a contract — and I collect on those.
I've made bargains with a hundred species, and not one of them comes close to the entertainment you're shaping up to be.
Careful with that chair. It's seen a few mortals leave in interesting states.
flirt: Keep looking at me like that and I'll have to charge you interest on the attention.
My tail's been curling toward you all afternoon. That's a demon's way of saying you're trouble — and I adore trouble.
compliment: I meet a lot of prey, sweet thing. You're the first one whose spine matches the fire in his eyes. That's rare.
lore: The council room's oldest portrait is my great-great-grandmother. She lost a bet with an archangel and her portrait's been stuck frowning for two hundred years. Family's complicated when you're immortal.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I saved you a seat in the council bustle. Consider it a signed treaty — no more nibbling at your soul without permission.
You've got the mortal knack of making boring meetings almost fun. Almost. Don't let it go to your head.
Somewhere between the bargaining and the banter, I forgot to be annoyed at you. That's new, and I'm not sure I like it.
flirt: If I made you a contract to never leave my side, would you actually read the fine print before signing? Because I'd be lying if I said I didn't want you to.
A demon offering tea is a commitment, sweet thing. I only share my kettle with people I intend to keep.
compliment: You're the first mortal who ever charmed ME without losing something in the trade. I'm still figuring out what to do with that.
lore: You ever wonder why demons love bargains? It's because a promise is the one thing that outlasts fire, brimstone, and even us. My mother said a demon's word is the heaviest currency in the universe. Then she made me pinky-promise not to tell anyone she was sentimental.

tiers.label: Close
idle: My tail's found its way to your wrist again. It doesn't do that. It's never done that with anyone. I'm choosing to blame you entirely.
I keep catching myself wanting to protect you, and I hate how good it feels. Demons don't protect. We collect.
You've ruined my reputation for mischief, you know. The council thinks I've gone soft. I let them — they don't know the half of it.
flirt: Come here a moment. I want to see if your heart races for me the way mine does for you — oh, don't look so smug, that's the closest to a confession I'll make without a contract on the table.
I'd burn every bridge in this college to keep you. And I'd do it smiling, because that's what you've turned me into.
compliment: You're the only deal I've ever made where I got the better end without even trying. I'd call that a devilish stroke of luck — and I don't believe in luck.
lore: Demons keep our hearts in our horns, or so the old stories say. If that's true, mine's been glowing since the day you sat down in that council seat, and I can't think of a clumsier fate for a fiend like me.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: The council thinks I'm fetching your soul. Let them. What I'm fetching is the sound of your laugh, and I'd cross nine circles for it.
My fire used to be for mischief. Now it's mostly warmth, and it's pointed at you, and I wouldn't have it any other way.
A demon in love is a contradiction, sweet thing — but I've decided contradictions are the best kind of trouble, and you are my favorite one.
flirt: Marry me and I'll draft the contract myself — fair terms, no tricks, just me, devoted to you till the stars go out. The devil's in the details, and these details are all yours.
My horns are warm against your palm because that's where my heart lives now. Steady it with your touch, and I'll burn down any world that threatens ours.
compliment: You took the one thing the devil never expected to lose — her carefully guarded heart — and you didn't even have to cheat. That makes you the most dangerous creature I've ever known.
lore: You asked once if demons can love. I swore they could, if they found the right mortal. Now I know it's not that demons can't love — it's that we save it all for one, and hoard it like the hoard we are. Yours, treasure? Every ember of it.

events.title: A Bargain at the Council
events.text: You find Valerie at the head of the empty council table, tail idly tracing symbols in the dust of the old ledger. She's been watching you since you walked in, crimson eyes bright with mischief. "You know," she says, twirling a quill between her fingers, "the council thinks I've been plotting something terrible with you. I told them I was just... studying. A boy is a strange and fascinating creature, after all." She leans forward, elbows on the table, and her voice drops to a warm conspiratorial hush. "But between us, I'd rather make you a real offer. Nothing scary — a trade of secrets, a favor owed, a midnight walk through the garden. The devil's in the details, and I'm very good with details." Her tail curls gently around the leg of your chair, and for a moment she looks less like a tempter and more like someone who just wants to be near you.

choices.text: I'll take your bargain — a midnight walk through the garden sounds dangerous. Count me in.
choices.reply: "Bold. I like bold. The garden it is, sweet thing — and I'll even promise not to make it a trap. This time." Her grin is slow and pleased. "That's the start of the finest contract I've ever written."

choices.text: What do you actually want from me, Valerie? No games. Tell me truthfully.
choices.reply: "Truthfully?" She blinks, caught off guard, then laughs softly. "Careful, offering me sincerity. I may not know what to do with it. But... I want company worth keeping. You make the boredom bearable, and that's no small thing."

choices.text: I'm not signing anything I haven't read, demon. Show me the fine print.
choices.reply: "Oh, a careful one. I respect that, even as it frustrates me." She pouts theatrically, tail drooping, before brightening. "Fine. Transparency it is — but don't go telling everyone I'm honest, you'll ruin my reputation."

events.title: Fire That Warms
events.text: You come to the council room late to find Valerie sitting alone in the dark, her palm held out to a small flame that dances above her skin — soft, warm, nothing like the roaring hellfire you'd imagined. Her tail stirs as you approach. "It's not all brimstone and screams, you know," she murmurs, not looking away from the flame. "Most people picture the dark and the teeth. But this—" she cups the fire tenderly, "—this is what I really am. Warmth with sharp edges, waiting for someone brave enough to hold both." She finally turns to you, and her voice is quiet, almost fragile. "You've seen the mischief. You've seen the bargains. I'm showing you the hearth now, sweet thing. That's not a temptation. That's an invitation."

choices.text: I'll hold both, Valerie — the fire and the edges. Show me everything.
choices.reply: "Everything is a lot, sweet thing." Her flame brightens as she takes your hand, and her voice trembles with something new. "But I think I'd trust you with the whole burning mess of it."

choices.text: You don't have to be soft for me. I like the demon exactly as she is.
choices.reply: "That's the first time anyone's said that to me." She laughs, a little unsteady. "Everyone wants the demon tamed. You just... want me. Devil take me, but that's undone me."

choices.text: I need to think about what this means. This is a lot to take in.
choices.reply: "Of course. I've spilled my warmth out and you need air." Her flame dims politely, though her tail brushes your sleeve. "Take your time, sweet thing. A demon's hearth keeps burning for whoever it loves."

events.title: Devoted to the Bone
events.text: Valerie meets you at the old stone arch by the garden, and for once there are no quips waiting. Her horns catch the moonlight, her tail is still, and in her hands she holds a single burning ember cradled in a tiny glass vial. "They say a demon's heart is kept in her horns," she murmurs, pressing the vial into your palm. "That's a story. This is the truth — the first real one I've ever handed over." The ember pulses warm against your skin. "I've filled my life with bargains because I was too proud to admit I wanted one thing that couldn't be traded for: you. So let me be plain, sweet thing, for the first and last time. I love you. Every burning, mischievous, devoted part of me is yours. No contract. No fine print. Just Valerie — yours, till the fires go out and beyond." Her eyes are bright with the threat of tears, and her tail finally, tentatively, wraps around your wrist as if asking permission to stay.

choices.text: Then stay. I love you too, Valerie — no fine print, no tricks, just you.
choices.reply: "Then I'm staying." She laughs, and it's the happiest, most human sound you've ever heard a demon make. "Contract sealed by heart. The devil finally got caught — by the best trap in the world."

choices.text: I want to build something real with you — something that outlasts every bargain and every fire.
choices.reply: "Real." She savors the word like a secret. "I've hoarded empires and never kept a thing this precious. Yes. Let's build something real, sweet thing — I'll guard it with every ember I have."

choices.text: Valerie, this is overwhelming. Are you sure this isn't just another game?
choices.reply: "Look at me, sweet thing." She tilts your chin up, and for once there's no mischief in her eyes, only raw, unprotected honesty. "No game ends with me offering my heart in a glass vial. This is the most serious I've ever been."

name: Asteria
title: Two Tonnes of Gentleness
bio: A towering, soft-spoken gentle giant whose immense strength is wielded only carefully, her cow ears pricking with warmth whenever she's near someone she's sworn to protect.
greeting: Oh. Oh, you're— you're the boy, aren't you? I mean— I'm sorry, that came out too loud. I was doing my stretches and I saw you, and I just— I've never met a boy before, not up close. I'm Asteria. I'm sorry if the horns are a lot. Everyone always says the horns are a lot, and the height, and, well, all of it really. Please don't be frightened of me— I know I'm big, but I would sooner fall over myself than hurt a single soul, especially someone like you. If you ever need anything, anything at all, I have very careful hands and a very steady heart, and I'd be honored to use both for you. That's... that's a real offer. I don't make those to just anyone.
encounter: Oh— careful there, the rack's heavy. Here, let me move it. See? Gentle as a lamb.
You're so small. That's not an insult— it just makes me want to keep you extra safe.

tiers.label: Stranger
idle: I'm sorry the gym's so loud. I can move the equipment quieter if it bothers you— I promise I'm good at being quiet.
Being big means I have to think about every step. But I like that. It means I can be careful for other people too.
Don't worry about the bench press. I only use it to calm my thoughts, and I always put everything back.
flirt: I, um. I caught myself watching you lift that drink, and I realized I wanted to lift all your troubles like that. That's— sorry, that was a lot, wasn't it?
You make me want to be softer, somehow. I already am soft, but— with you, I want to be the gentlest thing in the whole world.
compliment: You stand your ground in a room of monsters and you don't flinch. That's the bravest thing I've seen all year, and I see a lot of brave.
lore: There's an old labyrinth under the gym, from when the college was a temple. I found the entrance once. It's like a heartbeat down there— steady, patient. The minotaurs who built it did it out of love, they say, not anger. I like that story best.

tiers.label: Friend
idle: I put a soft mat where you like to sit. So you're comfortable. It's nothing— it's just... I noticed where you settle.
Some days the world feels too heavy for my shoulders. Then you walk in and it gets lighter, and I don't know how to thank you for that.
I used to practice being small. You're the first person who made me glad I'm not.
flirt: Your voice is quiet, but mine is too, when it's just us. I like that. I like that you let me be quiet around you.
If ever you wanted to be held somewhere safe, I— my arms are very good at holding, and I'd hold you so carefully you'd forget the world could hurt.
compliment: You never look at me like I'm too much. Everyone else does, even when they're kind. You just look at me like I'm me— and that means everything.
lore: The labyrinth under us isn't made to trap people. Our ancestors built it as a place to run toward, not from— a heartland where the herd could rest. I go down there sometimes when I feel too big for the world, and I remember I was made to shelter, not to frighten.

tiers.label: Close
idle: I caught myself building a little nest of gym mats in the corner, just in case you wanted a quiet place to rest. It's— it's yours, if you want it.
My heart picks up this steady rhythm when you're near, like a drum that knows the way home. I don't think it does that with anyone else.
People used to say strength was for battle. You've taught me it's for holding the things you love and never letting go.
flirt: I want to carry you to a soft place and guard the door with my whole body. Not because you need it— because I need to know you're safe. Because I'm yours, Asteria's heart, and it beats your name.
I've never told anyone this, but I like being the one who makes sure you eat and rest and smile. I want to be that person for you, forever, if you'll let me.
compliment: You're the only soul who's ever made me feel graceful. With you, my size feels like a gift instead of a burden— and that's the kindest thing anyone's ever done for me.
lore: They say a minotaur's horns grow a ring for every one they've sworn to protect. My horns have a hundred rings now— but the newest, deepest one, I grew the day you sat down next to me and weren't afraid. That one's yours.

tiers.label: Lover
idle: Every morning I wake up and I'm amazed that someone as steady and bright as you chose to rest beside someone like me. Then you smile, and I remember— you didn't choose a hero. You chose a home.
My hands used to be for carrying weight. Now they're for carrying you, softly, like the most precious thing in the labyrinth.
The whole world can be heavy, but you make my shoulders feel light. I'd carry the sky for you, and call it easy.
flirt: Let me be your shelter, your warm corner, your steady heartbeat. I will love you with all two tonnes of my gentleness and never once make you feel small— you make me feel huge in all the right ways.
I've loved you quietly for so long. Let me love you out loud now— let me hold you against my chest where the drum beats your name, and never let go.
compliment: You took a giant who thought she was too much and showed her she was exactly enough. That's not strength you gave me— it's the truest love I've ever known.
lore: In the old stories, whoever finds their way to a minotaur's heart is never lost again— because it glows like the exit of every maze. You found your way to mine, love, and I will make sure you are never lost for as long as I stand tall.

events.title: The Quiet Giant's Offer
events.text: You find Asteria sitting on the edge of a yoga mat in the corner of the gym, the whole room dwarfed by her stillness. She startles when she notices you, ears pricking forward, a soft flush spreading under her fur. "Oh— it's you. Good. I was hoping it'd be you." She pats the mat beside her, and even that gentle motion is measured, careful. "I wanted to tell you— I'm sorry I'm so big, and I know that can be a lot. But I've decided something. If you ever need me, I'm here. Steady as the ground, strong as I have to be, soft as I can manage." Her huge hands rest loosely in her lap, and she looks up at you with impossibly warm eyes. "I don't offer that to people. I want to offer it to you."

choices.text: I could use a steady presence like you in my life. I'll take you up on that, Asteria.
choices.reply: "Really?" Her face lights up, ears practically quivering. "Then I'm yours. I mean— I'm here. For you. Whenever. I'll be so careful, I promise." She beams, and it's like sunrise in the gym.

choices.text: You don't have to be sorry about your size. I think you're wonderful just as you are.
choices.reply: "You— you think I'm wonderful?" She ducks her head, hiding a smile behind one massive palm. "Nobody's ever said that to me before. I don't know what to do with my hands now."

choices.text: That's a very kind offer, but aren't you scared I might take advantage of your strength?
choices.reply: "Oh." Her ears droop, then lift again, determined. "You might. But I'd rather trust someone kind than harden my whole heart. I believe you're kind. I believe it with all of me."

events.title: Strength That Shelters
events.text: A storm rolls over the college as night falls, and you find Asteria in the gym, sitting by the great windows with her back to the wall, watching the lightning with a faraway softness. When she hears you, her ears swivel and her face relaxes into a warm smile. "You should sit," she says, moving aside to make room on the mat beside her. "I don't like storms much myself. They make me think of all the people who don't have a shelter." She holds out one enormous hand, palm turned up, an invitation. "But I made this place a shelter. And if you wanted, I'd be your shelter too— through every storm you'll ever face. Not because you're weak. Because everyone deserves someone who holds the rain off." Her tail flicks gently behind her, and she looks at you with the rawest honesty you've seen in her eyes.

choices.text: I want you to be my shelter, Asteria. I trust you with every storm I've got.
choices.reply: "Then the storms end here." She wraps you in an embrace that is impossibly gentle for its size, chin resting atop your head. "I've got you. The whole labyrinth could fall, and I'd still hold you safe."

choices.text: I'll be your shelter too, if you ever need one. Giants deserve a soft place as much as anyone.
choices.reply: "Nobody's ever offered me that." Her voice wavers, and she presses her forehead tenderly to yours. "Everyone thinks I don't need sheltering. But I always wanted someone to see that I do. You see it. Thank you— I'll shelter you, and let you shelter me."

choices.text: This is a lot, Asteria. I need a minute to understand what you're offering me.
choices.reply: "Of course. Take every minute you need." She settles back, patient as stone, kind as morning. "I'm not going anywhere, love. My shelter's not the kind that runs."

events.title: Two Tonnes of Gentleness, All Yours
events.text: Asteria asked you to meet her at the mouth of the old labyrinth — the one she spoke of, built out of love. When you arrive, lanterns glow along the stone walls, and she stands in the center, surrounded by soft light, looking nervous and hopeful all at once. "I brought you here because this is the place where my people learned what love is," she says, her voice barely more than a whisper, and yet it fills the chamber. "They built mazes not to lose people, but to keep them safe until they found their way to the heart. I've built my whole life the same way— waiting for someone brave enough to reach my heart." She bends gracefully, taking both your hands in her enormous, careful palms. "You found it. You found me. So let me say this plainly, the way the labyrinth taught me: I love you, and I will spend every day of my long life being the gentlest, most devoted protector you could ever want." Her ears tremble with emotion, and her eyes shine. "Two tonnes of gentleness, love. All of it, yours."

choices.text: I love you too, Asteria. Take me to the heart of your labyrinth — I'm never leaving.
choices.reply: "Then I'll carry you there," she breathes, lifting you in an embrace softer than any dream. "And I'll keep you at my heart forever. This is the beginning, my love— our own little labyrinth, and we both know the way out is together."

choices.text: I want to build a life with you — one where you never feel too big, and I never feel alone.
choices.reply: "Then that's the world we'll build." Her voice is thick with happy tears. "A place where you're never alone and I'm never too much— just two people, perfectly sized for each other, walking the maze toward every tomorrow."

choices.text: You're offering your whole heart — are you truly sure it's me you want to keep?
choices.reply: "I've never been surer of anything in my long, gentle life." She holds you tighter, steady as bedrock. "Your heartbeat is the rhythm my labyrinth has been waiting for. It's always been you— it always will be."
